title: Westinghouse to qualify BWXT for AP1000 component manufacture
html:
Westinghouse has awarded manufacturing qualification contracts to BWXT for the fabrication of demonstration pieces for steam generators in BWXT's Cambridge, Ontario, facility in Canada and reactor vessel internals in its facility in York, Pennsylvania. Qualification will allow Westinghouse and BWXT to collaborate to enable the manufacturing of large-scale, nuclear-grade components in Canada and the USA for AP1000 projects globally, the companies said.

BWXT recently completed a CAD80 million (USD56 million) expansion of its Cambridge facility, significantly expanding its capacity to manufacture large-scale nuclear components for both conventional and advanced reactors of all sizes.

The agreement reflects the confidence global reactor vendors have in the capabilities that exist in Canada and the USA, BWXT's President of Commercial Operations, John MacQuarrie, said. "As a merchant supplier, we're expanding our ability to manufacture large, nuclear-grade components, developing specialised skills and creating capacity that can support nuclear projects in Canada, the US and around the world," he added.

"Canada's world-class nuclear industry has the expertise, workforce and manufacturing capabilities needed to support the growing global demand for new nuclear energy," President of Westinghouse Canada John Gorman said. "By combining BWXT Canada's capabilities with Westinghouse's AP1000 technology and global experience, we are creating new opportunities for Canadian industry to support nuclear projects at home and around the world."

Six AP1000 reactors are in operation in the USA and China and 14 are under construction in China. Further units are under various contract phases around the world, including in Poland, Ukraine, and Bulgaria. Westinghouse is owned by Brookfield and Cameco.
summary: Westinghouse Electric Company and BWXT Canada have agreed to qualify BWXT Canada to manufacture key components for AP1000 projects, a move the companies say expands opportunities for the Canadian and US nuclear supply…
